blocks.content: Describe electrical buses and distribution concepts in aircraft.

items.definition: An electrical bus is a common conductive distribution point connected to one or more power sources (battery, alternator) and multiple loads (avionics, lights, systems). All loads connected to the bus share the same voltage source.
items.analogy: Like a power strip — one plug into the wall (power source), many devices plugged in (loads), all sharing the same supply.

items.definition: The DC electrical system supplies power to all electrically-powered equipment: avionics (radios, navigation, flight instruments), lighting, ignition systems, fuel pumps, and other electrical loads — during all phases of flight from pre-start through shutdown.
items.analogy: The aircraft's DC system is like the bloodstream of the aircraft's electrical life — everything that needs power gets it from here.

items.definition: The DC electrical system in a GA aircraft powers: avionics (radios, navigation equipment), lighting (position lights, landing lights, interior), ignition systems, electric fuel pump, and any other electrically-operated equipment.
items.analogy: The DC system is the electrical utility network of the aircraft — like the electrical panel in a house powering everything from the refrigerator to the lights.

blocks.question: What is an aircraft electrical bus?
choices: A dedicated cable that connects the battery directly to each load
A protective device that interrupts power during faults
A voltage regulation device for sensitive avionics
A common distribution point that supplies power from one or more sources to multiple loads
blocks.feedback: A bus is a distribution node: power comes in from sources (battery, alternator) and goes out to all connected loads. Multiple buses allow circuit separation — essential loads on one bus, non-essential on another — for fault tolerance.

blocks.question: What is the primary purpose of an aircraft's DC electrical system?
choices: To convert AC power from the alternator into usable DC
To supply power to avionics, lights, ignition, fuel systems, and electrical equipment during all phases of operation
To charge the battery only when the alternator is operating at cruise RPM
To distribute power solely to flight-critical instruments
blocks.feedback: The DC electrical system serves as the backbone of all electrical power distribution — from pre-start checks through engine shutdown. It powers both flight-critical and non-critical electrical loads at all times.

blocks.question: In a general aviation aircraft, what does the DC electrical system primarily power?
choices: Only flight-critical instruments and the battery charger
Avionics, lighting, ignition systems, and other electrical equipment
Only lighting and the electric fuel pump
blocks.feedback: The DC system is comprehensive — it powers all electrical loads: avionics, all lighting systems, ignition, fuel pump, and miscellaneous electrical equipment. GA aircraft have very few non-electrical systems.
